scores.critique: Strongest solver design: 10 substeps x 1 GS iteration with lambda reset (correct Macklin-2019 form), Bergou isometric K-vector/coef formulas are correct (K=[c03+c04,c01+c02,-c01-c03,-c02-c04], L=0 for flat rest; note coef 3/(2(A0+A1)) carries an extra 1/2 vs Bergou, harmless), Macklin-2014 friction correctly transcribed, smin(k=0.04) blending at joints removes gradient discontinuities, gravity ramp + 5x damping during sewing, rest-length (not stiffness) seam ramp, velocity clamp (5 m/s -> 8.3 mm/substep) consistent with the 0.5h displacement clamp and the tunnelling argument, layer offsets, in-app runAcceptance(). Concrete errors: (1) Bend compliance table is off by orders of magnitude. With C = 1/2 coef |L|^2 on a 15 mm hinge folded 0.5 rad, |L| = 2h sin(theta/2) = 7.4e-3 m, C ~ 0.21, |grad C| ~ 66, restoring force C*gradC/alpha ~ 2.8 N for cotton alpha=5 vs ~1.6e-4 N physical (B~5e-6 N.m) -> cotton drapes like cardboard, chiffon (300) still ~300x too stiff; and because C is already quadratic in x the XPBD energy is quartic (mushy for small wrinkles, brick-like for folds). (2) Boundary-repair inserts a midpoint on one edge only: on a seam edge this silently breaks the equal-vertex-count pairing invariant (the acceptance check #1 will catch it late). (3) Free-edge sample count round(L/h) is 0 for edges < 0.5h -> collapsed edge; seam max(2,...) only protects seams; round can also yield 1.4h segments whose diametral circle (0.7h) exceeds the 0.55h clearance so the Gabriel guarantee fails. (4) SDF bake estimate 150-300 ms for 580k cells x ~25 primitives with smin is optimistic in JS (0.7-1.5 s) without a per-cell primitive cull. (5) Mixed units inside body.params (cm, metres for height, 0..1 blends) plus mm size rows is the worst conflict surface among the three for 8 agents. (6) Sample front piece has mirrorAxis:'x' with full-width vertices [-240,240] -> reflection would double it. (7) A1 (bezier+polygon+offset+delaunay+remesh+pack) is the critical-path bottleneck for A2, A4 and A6. (8) Friction uses pen = r-d, which is ~0 for resting vertices, so static friction on shoulders is weak (shared by all three).

Best pattern-making fidelity (per-edge allowance with hem square-off, fold edges, per-point grade deltas, grade nest, ease % readout, piece-measurement CSV) and the only candidate whose bending numbers are physically calibrated (cross-vertex distance: cotton 5e-2, denim 5e-3, silk 1 m/N match B ~ 5e-6/1.5e-4/1e-6 N.m within a few x). Ramanujan closed-form radius is correct. Concrete errors: (1) Collision perf claim is wrong by 10-30x: analytic min-union SDF queried per particle per substep with 3-tap finite-difference normals means ~6000 x 8 x (AABB test over ~25 prims + ~6 full evals x 4 for FD) ~ 1M+ primitive evaluations/frame, 20-60 ms in JS, not 'under 2 ms'; loft queries also do a binary search each. Needs a baked grid or analytic gradients + culling. (2) Min-union with no smin -> normal discontinuities at armpit/crotch -> jitter. (3) Torso loft is a superellipse (e=2.4 at chest) but radii are solved from the Ramanujan ellipse perimeter: superellipse perimeter is ~3-5% larger, so acceptance check 5 ('measure within 0.5%') will fail by construction unless measure.js is a numeric perimeter with correction. (4) 'alpha_stretch scaled by 1/edgeLength' is a unit muddle: for a 2D spring lattice the per-edge stiffness is already resolution independent (k ~ E t), and alpha/L makes 15 mm edges ~67x softer than the table implies (cotton ~4% strain). (5) 5 cm/substep displacement clamp is inert (25 m/s at h=2 ms) and larger than an arm radius; the velocity clamp is applied after the velocity update so it does not bound the current substep's move. (6) After sewing, 'positions averaged each substep' ignores invMass (drags pins) and is redundant with the alpha=0 constraint. (7) No self-collision in v1: sleeve/torso and collar layers will interpenetrate in the flagship demo. (8) Segment model duplicates endpoints (p1 of i == p0 of i+1) -> invariant every tool and __app.updatePiece patch must maintain. (9) Non-seam edges use round(len/h) -> 0 segments for short edges. (10) Pop-out streams 60 Hz frames plus pick/pin forwarding and a heartbeat -> more integration surface than needed; acceptance check 12 (popup document.title) is flaky under automation. (11) Sample says '5 seams ... = 8 seams'.

Cleanest contracts for parallel agents: unit-suffixed params (chest_cm), compact hIn/hOut outline (no duplicated endpoints), ClothMesh with edges/bendPairs/seamPairs/uv/edgeSamples, single wiring.js integration point, drape() on load, sim.step(n) returning stats, ui.click(id). Mesher is the most correct: max(1,ceil(L/h)) sampling (true Gabriel guarantee with 0.6h clearance), seam edge chains with proportional arclength matching, midpoint insertion mirrored onto the partner chain (keeps parity), Laplacian smoothing with flip check. Body: consistent ellipse (e=2) + Ramanujan bisection, IQ sdRoundCone, 10 mm baked grid with bounding-sphere pre-cull, debounced rebake with old grid kept until swap, mergeGeometries is the correct r180 addon name. Physics: CCD-lite sign-flip check, seam-neighbour self-collision mask, snapshot restore, in-place compliance rewrite. Concrete errors: (1) quantity:2 + flip instancing leaves seam->instance addressing undefined (seam.a.piece:'sleeve' cannot say which sleeve meets which armhole); A1/A3/A5 will each invent a rule. (2) Bend compliance table (cotton 4e-4 m/N) is ~500x too stiff: cross-vertex delta for a 0.5 rad fold is ~8e-4 m -> 2 N restoring vs ~1.6e-4 N physical; energy is quartic in angle as for all distance bending. (3) 6 substeps (adaptive drop to 4) is low for 1-iteration XPBD; stiff fabrics will look soft and seams take longer to settle; vMax 8 m/s = 22 mm/substep against a 4 mm collision offset and a 10 mm grid relies entirely on the sign-flip check. (4) Min-union SDF with no smin -> jitter at armpit/crotch. (5) Central-difference gradient of a trilinear field (6 extra samples) is coarser than the analytic trilinear gradient and 7x the cost. (6) Pattern space y-down while outlines are declared CCW: orientation sign and 'right-hand normal' in offset.js will be read differently by A2 and A7 unless pinned in types.js. (7) Single seamAllowance per piece (no hem/neck distinction). (8) 10 agents raise coordination cost; core/geometry.js is a Phase-1 A1 deliverable but a Phase-1 dependency for A2/A3/A7. (9) Acceptance 13 clicks canvas at 'known mm->px coordinates' but no mm->px helper is exposed; check 12 (popup) is flaky. (10) Sample says '5 seams ... 8 seams'.

grafts: From product-first: seam sides as edge chains (`edges:[...]`) with proportional-arclength sample distribution and corner/notch samples forced, so sleeve-head-to-armhole seams do not require edge splitting.

From product-first: boundary repair must insert the midpoint on BOTH seam partners at the same fraction; sampling uses max(1, ceil(L/h)) so segments are <= h and the Gabriel/0.6h argument actually holds.
From product-first: two Laplacian smoothing passes on interior vertices with per-vertex orientation-flip rejection; Euler/CCW/boundary-edge post-validation and h*=1.3 retry before failing.
From product-first: unit-suffixed parameter names (chest_cm, seamAllowance_mm, offset_mm) in every JSON field and typedef; no bare numbers with implied units.
From product-first: debounced (150 ms) SDF rebake with the physics colliding against the old grid until the new one is atomically swapped; bounding-sphere pre-cull per cell during bake.
From product-first: CCD-lite — if sdf sign flips between xPrev and x within a substep, project to the xPrev side; snapshot the state every 60 sane frames and restore on NaN.
From product-first: self-collision mask for vertex pairs within 2 rings of a seam; fabric change rewrites compliance arrays in place with no rebuild.

From product-first: `sim.step(n)` runs n frames synchronously with rendering suppressed and returns the stats object; `drape()` (= arrange + sew + play) is the default on load; `ui.click(id)`; single app/wiring.js as the only place modules are connected.
From product-first: ClothMesh contract carrying edges, bendPairs (4-tuples), seamPairs, pieceOfVertex, uv and per-edge vertex lists so physics and render never re-derive topology.

From patternmaking-first: physically calibrated bending values as the reference (B in N.m: cotton ~5e-6, denim ~1.5e-4, silk ~1e-6, chiffon ~3e-7, wool ~2e-5, leather ~1e-3) and the Stiffness/Drape/Weight log-linear sliders for non-physicists.
From patternmaking-first: per-edge seam allowance with fold edges (allowance 0, 'PLACE ON FOLD'), hem square-off rule, and output validation (simple polygon, area > stitch area, miter fallback).

From patternmaking-first: per-point grade deltas keyed by size (interpolated by row index) on top of driver scaling, notches re-derived by t, seam-ease drift check per size, grade-nest SVG, piece-measurement CSV.
From patternmaking-first: push any arranged particle with d<0 out along the SDF normal before the first step; seam ease % readout in the status bar; per-module selftest.js runnable from __app.
From patternmaking-first: Sloan-style edge-flip recovery as an alternative that never changes vertex counts (keeps seam parity) if midpoint insertion loops.
corrections: Bending compliance tables in physics-first (cotton 5, chiffon 300) and product-first (cotton 4e-4 m/N) are 10^2-10^4 x too stiff; both formulations (C=1/2 x^T Q x and cross-vertex distance) also give quartic energy in angle. Use C = |L| * sqrt(3/(A0+A1)) (i.e. sqrt(x^T Q x)) so the XPBD energy is quadratic and alpha_bend = 1/B with B in N.m from the Kawabata ranges above; skip the constraint when |L| < 1e-9 and never allow alpha_bend = 0 (0/0 at flat).
Boundary-repair midpoint insertion on a seam edge must also be applied to the partner chain at the same arclength fraction; otherwise equal-vertex-count pairing breaks (physics-first §3 step 3).
Sample counts: never round(L/h) (gives 0 for edges < 0.5h and 1.4h segments that violate the 0.55h Gabriel clearance); use max(1, ceil(L/h)) for free edges and max(2, ceil(max(LA,LB)/h)) for seams.

Do not query an analytic min-union SDF with finite-difference normals per particle per substep (patternmaking-first): that is ~1M primitive evaluations per frame (20-60 ms), not 2 ms. Bake to a uniform grid (10-15 mm) with the analytic trilinear gradient, cull primitives per cell during the bake, and use a coarse grid while sliders drag.
Use polynomial smin (k ~ 0.04 m) at joints (arm/shoulder, thigh/pelvis, neck/torso) — plain min-union produces normal discontinuities at armpit and crotch that cause persistent jitter.

Do not solve torso radii from the Ramanujan ellipse perimeter while lofting a superellipse with e != 2 (patternmaking-first): perimeters differ by 3-5% so a 0.5% measurement acceptance fails by construction. Either use e=2 with Ramanujan, or compute the superellipse perimeter numerically (homogeneous degree 1 => scale linearly).

Do not scale stretch compliance by 1/edgeLength: per-edge spring stiffness in a 2D lattice is already resolution independent; alpha/L makes 15 mm edges ~67x softer than tabulated. Likewise the '(h/15)^2' bend rescale is unnecessary for the Bergou energy, which is mesh-consistent.

Displacement clamp and velocity clamp must agree and be smaller than the thinnest limb's medial radius: ~5 m/s and ~8 mm/substep at h=1/600 s. A 5 cm/substep clamp (patternmaking-first) is inert; 8 m/s at 6 substeps (product-first, 22 mm/substep against a 4 mm offset) relies entirely on the sign-flip check. Apply the velocity clamp before the position prediction, not only after.

Do not weld sewn pairs by averaging positions (ignores invMass, drags pinned vertices, redundant with the alpha~0 constraint). Keep the distance constraint with rest 0 and the |x_i-x_j|<1e-9 skip guard.
Piece instancing (quantity:2 + flip) requires an explicit instance index in SeamSide (or auto-derived mirrored seams); left/right sleeve-to-armhole pairing must be defined in types.js before fan-out.
Keep the seam ramp as a rest-length ramp L(t) = d0(1 - t/T) with alpha ~ 1e-5..1e-9, never a stiffness ramp; T=1.0 s with gravity ramp and elevated damping during sewing.

Static friction based on pen = r - d is ~0 for resting vertices; evaluate friction against the pre-projection normal displacement (or treat contact within offset + ~1 mm as active) so cloth does not creep off shoulders.
Do not put body params in mixed units (cm + m + 0..1 in one object, physics-first). All JSON fields carry a unit suffix; 3D is metres, pattern is mm, size charts are mm.

Include self-collision (vertex-vertex spatial hash, counting sort, 1-ring exclusion, seam-neighbour mask, run every 2nd substep) in v1; 'layers interpenetrate' in the flagship T-shirt is not acceptable.

Use >= 8-10 substeps x 1 iteration; an adaptive drop to 4 substeps visibly softens stiff fabrics and seams. Pop-out and popup-title checks must not be blocking acceptance items (popups are flaky under automation); expose a mm->px helper before any canvas-click acceptance test.

Sample garment seam counts are miscounted in two candidates ('5 seams ... = 8'); the T-shirt has 8 seams (2 shoulder, 2 side, 2 sleeve underarm, 2 sleeve head) — verify with the mesher's edge lengths in Phase 0.
